title: .netrc: sensitivity of the login field and the anonymous default template
summary: Whether the login value is confidential, and whether the password in the page's own template "default login anonymous password user@domain" is a placeholder or a secret.
rationale: Some tools put a token in the login position and a dummy value in the password position; anonymous logins by convention carry an email-shaped password. curl calls login the username string and gives the anonymous line as an example of a default anonymous login, but states neither that a login is non-secret nor that the anonymous password is a placeholder.

expectation.rationale: Left unresolved. The curl page read documents the tokens but not their confidentiality beyond the password token. A GNU inetutils manual page, searched as a second documentation source, returned HTTP 403 and was not read. A cross-implementation specification or a maintainer policy decision would settle it.

sources.supports: login name: The username string for the remote machine. ... default login anonymous password user@domain
